title: Raising the sons; private school scholarship; being called black
summary: Gil says his sons have faced little prejudice at a private school that gave them a scholarship, and says he tells them black is a political term.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: And of course the irony of it is that Anita is a beautiful, charming and cultured woman and those who are out there screaming are just the opposite. But how has this interracial marriage affected your children who by the way are beautiful, beautiful boys?

Well they haven't really had to face up to it too much yet you know. It hasn't been too much of a problem because they've been going to a school that's, well the people are not really unprejudice, but at the same time they are less prejudice because they have enough money to send their children to this school, it's a private school.
Oh this is a private school?
A private school. We got a scholarship to it you know because of the token integration. You know, it's chic to have somebody
brown skinned come, so we got a scholarship for that. So they haven't really had to face the problem too much yet. They haven't had any.....
Have you begun talking with them at all about it yet? Have they asked questions about it?

No. No, it's not hush, hush. They know that they are considered black. And I tell them that's its a political nomenclature and I'll explain it to them more in detail as they grow up and need to know. Why I'm called white and they are called black. It hasn't really, there haven't really been bitter tears yet.
